body:
## Security Finding

**Severity**: low
**Type**: unsafe-pattern (a manual run of the ISO workflow on any branch signs the ISO and replaces the public download)

Risk: security posture (the change is in `.github/workflows/build-iso.yml`, and this lane's token cannot push workflow files). There is no choice to make here; the replacement below is the whole change. It needs a lane whose token can push workflow files, or a maintainer.

`build-iso.yml` can be started by hand (`workflow_dispatch`) on any branch. Its `skip_upload` input defaults to `false`, and the `publish` job has no condition on the ref:

```yaml
  publish:
    name: Publish verified ISO
    needs: build-and-publish
    if: ${{ inputs.skip_upload != true && github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
```

`pull_request` is not a trigger of this workflow, so the second half of that condition is always true. A run on a feature branch therefore:

1. builds the ISO from that branch's `tromso/`, `iso.justfile`, `Justfile` and workflow file;
2. signs it with the workflow's keyless identity (`…/build-iso.yml@refs/heads/<branch>`);
3. uploads it to R2 as `tromso/tromso-live-latest.iso` with its `.sig`, `.cert` and checksum, which is the public nightly download (`https://download.tunaos.org/tromso/tromso-live-latest.iso`). The `Determine channel` step treats every branch other than `stable` as nightly.

The image build already has this guard: `build-final.yml` logs in, pushes and scans only under `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/stable'`.

The self-check that runs after signing has the same gap. Its comment says "Verify with the documented consumer command before any upload", and its pattern stops at `build-iso\.yml@`, so it passes for a certificate from any branch.

Checked at `main` = `7bbfd3b`. Not run: I did not start the workflow.

## Impact

- Someone who tests an ISO change with "Run workflow" on their branch, and leaves the default input, replaces the public nightly ISO with a build of unreviewed code. The boot check still has to pass, but nothing in the run says the download was replaced.
- The same path works on purpose for any account or token that can push a branch and start a workflow. Such an account can also change the workflow file on its branch, so this guard is not a boundary against it. It removes the accident, and it makes the workflow on `main` sign only what `main` built.
- Together with #494 (the README and runbook patterns), a signature that passes the documented check then always means "built and signed from `main`".

## Recommendation

Exact replacement, against `7bbfd3b`. Two lines change in the workflow, and one invariant is added.

- The `publish` job runs only when `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`. The guard is on the job, not on the steps, so `test_iso_publication_event_gates_fail_closed` (which evaluates the step conditions) needs no change. Every automatic path keeps working: the `push` trigger is limited to `main`, a `workflow_run` run has the default branch as its ref, and `promote-stable.yml` calls this workflow from a scheduled run on `main`. The published nightly certificate confirms it: `tromso-live-latest.iso.cert` (issued 2026-11-13) names `…/build-iso.yml@refs/heads/main`.
- The self-check uses the pattern that #494 puts in `README.md`, so the workflow verifies with the documented command. `\$` keeps the `$` literal inside the double quotes.

```diff
--- a/.github/workflows/build-iso.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/build-iso.yml
@@ -245,7 +245,7 @@ jobs:
   publish:
     name: Publish verified ISO
     needs: build-and-publish
-    if: ${{ inputs.skip_upload != true && github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
+    if: ${{ inputs.skip_upload != true && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
     permissions:
       actions: read
@@ -319,7 +319,7 @@ jobs:
           cosign verify-blob "$ISO" \
             --certificate "${ISO}.cert" \
             --signature "${ISO}.sig" \
-            --certificate-identity-regexp "^https://github\.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/\.github/workflows/build-iso\.yml@" \
+            --certificate-identity-regexp "^https://github\.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/\.github/workflows/build-iso\.yml@refs/heads/main\$" \
             --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
           echo "sig_path=${ISO}.sig" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           echo "cert_path=${ISO}.cert" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

Add this to `tests/pytest/test_iso_invariants.py`, before `test_iso_signing_preserves_detached_outputs_with_cosign3` (`REPO` and `re` are already defined at the top of that file):

```python
def test_iso_is_signed_and_published_only_from_main():
    """A manual run on another branch must not sign or replace the public ISO."""
    workflow = (REPO / ".github/workflows/build-iso.yml").read_text()
    publish = workflow.split("\n  publish:\n", 1)[1]
    condition = re.search(r"^    if:\s*\$\{\{(.*?)\}\}", publish, re.MULTILINE)[1]
    assert "github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'" in condition
    assert "||" not in condition
    # The self-check is the README command: only a certificate from main passes.
    verify = publish.split("cosign verify-blob", 1)[1].split("- name:", 1)[0]
    assert r"build-iso\.yml@refs/heads/main\$" in verify
```

`AGENTS.md` asks for a row in the troubleshooting table of `docs/ci-and-iso-pipeline.md` with each ISO invariant. This row passes the Prose check (`ste-lint --max 0`):

```
| 2026-11-20 | A manual run of `build-iso.yml` on a different branch signs the ISO and replaces `tromso-live-latest.iso` | The `publish` job had no condition on the ref, and `skip_upload` is `false` by default | The `publish` job runs only for `refs/heads/main`. Its self-check uses the README pattern; `test_iso_is_signed_and_published_only_from_main` |
```

Tested here on a copy of `7bbfd3b`: with the workflow change and the test, `pytest tests/pytest/` gives 366 passed (365 before; the same three `test_release_boot_keys.py` tests fail before and after because this machine has no `make`). With only the test applied, `test_iso_is_signed_and_published_only_from_main` fails. `actionlint` and `zizmor` were not run here. The change keeps every `uses:` line, so `actions.lock` does not change.

The workflow edit and the test have to land together, because the test is red until the guard is there. This change does not depend on #494 and can merge before or after it.

One thing this does not cover, noted so it is not lost: `build-final.yml` and `build-iso.yml` also publish for `refs/heads/stable`. That branch does not exist today and no ruleset covers the name, so the reviewed workflows would publish `:stable` and the stable ISO channel for anyone who creates a branch with that name and starts a build. Stable promotion no longer needs that path (`promote-stable.yml` copies the digest that `main` built), so it can be removed, or the name can get a ruleset; that is a separate change and is not part of this issue.

- [ ] the `publish` job in `build-iso.yml` runs only for `refs/heads/main`
- [ ] the self-check after signing ends with `@refs/heads/main$`
- [ ] `test_iso_is_signed_and_published_only_from_main` is in `tests/pytest/test_iso_invariants.py`
